C-KERNEL-CAPABILITY-PROVIDER-TARGETING-2.IntentSummary:
Deliver the approved generic platform capability provider targeting enhancement in `worldline-kernel`. This change enables callers to target a specific `InstallationId` when obtaining and invoking a capability handle, solving the multi-installation shadowing gap identified during C-BROWSER-SEARCH-PROVIDERS-20260904 feasibility analysis.
Targeting binds to durable `InstallationId`, not ephemeral `RuntimeId`. The broker resolves the live runtime at admission time without authority inheritance across restarts. If a targeted installation is absent, stopped, quarantined, or incompatible, invocation fails closed with an explicit typed error (`TargetUnavailable`) without silent fallback. No preferred-provider tables or selection policy persistence are added to the microkernel. Clean backward compatibility is maintained for untargeted invocations.
Admission is codex_led on branch codex/kernel-capability-provider-targeting-20260905. The approved spec is the normative change boundary; design-context.xml is non-normative.

T-001.Title: Define CapabilityTarget model, target-aware registry resolution, and draft the ADR

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: Define `CapabilityTarget` enum (`AnyCompatible`, `Installation(InstallationId)`) in `crates/worldline-kernel/src/capability.rs` and re-export in `lib.rs`.
Implement target-aware candidate resolution and selection in `CapabilityRegistry` supporting explicit `InstallationId` filtering alongside compatibility matching.
Define typed `TargetUnavailable` failure representations in `crates/worldline-kernel/src/error.rs` and `rpc.rs`.
Add unit tests in `crates/worldline-kernel/src/capability.rs` verifying targeted filtering selects the exact installation and returns None on absent/incompatible targets.
Create draft `docs/adr/ADR-KERNEL-CAPABILITY-PROVIDER-TARGETING-V1.md` documenting targeting principles, failure semantics, and microkernel invariants.

T-002.Title: Implement broker targeted invocation, handle constructors, and public kernel APIs

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: Add `target: CapabilityTarget` to `CapabilityHandle` and `InvocationRequest`, defaulting untargeted requests to `CapabilityTarget::AnyCompatible`.
Implement `CapabilityHandle::targeted`, `handle.target()`, and target-aware `handle.is_available()`.
Implement `Kernel::capability_for_installation(caller, capability, installation_id)` in `crates/worldline-kernel/src/kernel.rs`.
Implement `ActivationContext::capability_for_installation(capability, installation_id)` in `crates/worldline-kernel/src/plugin.rs`.
Update `InvocationBroker::invoke` to resolve target provider via target-aware selection; return `CapabilityError::TargetUnavailable` without silent fallback on target failure.
Enforce standard caller capability authorization check regardless of targeting; lack of grant results in `Denied`.
Record requested target installation ID, resolved runtime ID, and outcome in trajectory security audit events without leaking invocation payloads.

Add acceptance tests in `crates/worldline-kernel/tests/runtime_v1_acceptance.rs` proving two active installations of the same capability can be targeted and invoked independently without provider-name branching in callers.
Prove that untargeted `capability_for` retains deterministic default resolution to the lowest InstallationId when multiple installations are active.
Prove that restarting a targeted installation creates a new `RuntimeId` and subsequent targeted invocations resolve to the fresh runtime without stale authority inheritance.
Prove strict fail-closed semantics: targeted invocation of absent, stopped, quarantined, or incompatible installation returns explicit typed error with zero silent fallback to other active providers.
Prove that caller capability authorization is strictly required for targeted handles; unprivileged caller receives `Denied`.
Prove trajectory security events record target installation ID, resolved runtime ID, and outcome code.
